claim: Current live Linux state and read-only A/B metadata can identify whether missing successful-boot acknowledgement is a repeat-fallback risk.
oracle: Fresh serial response, current slot from bootconfig, parsed devinfo header and B flags, boot-success service status; no partition writes. Do not attribute a specific reset without reset evidence.

user_journey.scenario: User reports recovery/Fastboot after repeated Linux tests; locate current OS without another forced reboot and show actual desktop.
user_journey.expected: Visible Omarchy if current session is healthy; clear report of remaining boot reliability gap.

invariants: Read devinfo only by verified PARTNAME
Read only first128bytes; output version and slot flags only
No setrw, boot flag changes, flash or reboot
Reference Google-derived upstream offsets; unsupported magic/version stop decoding
gitnexus: Standalone firmware metadata diagnostic outside workspace graph; inspect boot-success shell and C offsets directly
ast: Python struct.unpack fields, strict magic/version gate

unit.red: Malformed header or unknown layout must fail closed
unit.green: Synthetic 3.15 header with independently specified slot bytes decodes correctly

faults: Transport absent: no waiting fastboot mutation
Mismatch between reported screen and live state: report both, prioritize fresh evidence

evidence: Current fresh serial reports Linux7.3,systemd,750us,renderD128,Hyprland and touch bound; no active CPU experiment timer/watchdog.
limitations: Read-only diagnosis does not fix boot persistence
Screenshot does not prove physical touch or scanout
No claim that all prior Google boots have the same cause
exit_gate: Verified read-only state plus source comparison; separate reviewed recovery plan before any boot metadata write.
